clue.text: If lost, they may well be broken

definitions.text: If lost, they may well be broken

parts.words: If lost, they may well be broken
parts.note: people who lose their affections to someone, and are then rejected, end up nursing broken ones

explanation.surface: A rueful remark about things that suffer damage once they go missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lost' points to falling in love: to lose your heart is to fall for someone, and a jilted lover's heart is said to be broken.
explanation.definitionFit: Organs of love are figuratively lost when people fall in love and broken when love ends.

clue.text: Where a bowler may go when taken off

definitions.text: Where a bowler may go when taken off

parts.words: Where a bowler may go when taken off
parts.note: a bowler is also a hard round felt hat, which is hung on a stand of pegs once removed

explanation.surface: Sounds like a cricket captain resting a bowler and sending him to the field or pavilion.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a bowler is 'taken off' when replaced; here the bowler is a hat, taken off the head and hung up.
explanation.definitionFit: A stand or set of hooks for hanging headwear is where a removed bowler hat would be put.

clue.text: A hole in one, perhaps, for mariner's dependant

definitions.meaning: in golf, a score three under par on a hole; a hole in one on a par-four hole is such a score
in Coleridge's Rime of the Ancient Mariner the seabird he shot was hung from his neck

explanation.surface: A golfing feat somehow linked to a sailor's dependant.
explanation.walkthrough: The golf sense is rarer than eagle or birdie: three under par. The mariner is Coleridge's Ancient Mariner, with the dead bird hanging from him.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: the golf score three below par, and the seabird hung around the Ancient Mariner's neck.

clue.text: They hold an alternative, but not in practice

indicators.note: the word They holds the alternative inside it, keeping it between its letters

parts.note: or is the word that introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: People who keep another option in reserve without ever putting it into action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hold' reads as 'believe', as in holding an opinion, but it is the container signal. The definition plays on the stock contrast between principle and practice.
explanation.definitionFit: Something true in principle rather than reality is said to hold in hypothesis, as opposed to in practice.

clue.text: On entering Canada, tumbled into the Snake

indicators.note: the combined letters fall about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone arriving in Canada falls into the Snake River.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entering' signals the container and 'tumbled' the anagram of the result; 'Snake' with its capital looks like a river's name but is the plain definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A large South American constricting serpent is a well-known kind of snake.

clue.text: It's twelve, anyway

indicators.note: read any way, forwards or backwards, the letters stay the same

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A shrug: it's twelve o'clock, whatever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'anyway' is read as 'any way': the word reads the same in either direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Midday is twelve o'clock.

clue.text: Escorted out — or stayed?

indicators.note: the letters of Escorted are put out of their order

explanation.surface: Was the guest shown out, or did they stay on?
explanation.walkthrough: 'stayed' looks like 'remained'; it means fitted with stays, the stiff ribs in a corset.
explanation.definitionFit: Stays are the boned strips of a corset, so a figure laced into one is stayed.

clue.text: Is involved in one dreadful row

indicators.note: Is goes inside the rearranged letters
the word one is made dreadful, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is caught up in one terrible quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dreadful' signals the anagram and 'involved in' the container. 'row' is the din sense, rhyming with cow, not a line or a boat trip.
explanation.definitionFit: A loud row is a racket or din, a synonym of loud sound.

clue.text: Sailors tear out side by side

indicators.note: the letters are put out of their order

explanation.surface: Sailors rush out together, shoulder to shoulder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges ABS and TEAR together.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving level with one another, in a line across, is a synonym of side by side.

clue.text: It may be taken to promote good feeling

definitions.text: It may be taken to promote good feeling

parts.words: It may be taken to promote good feeling
parts.note: a pill swallowed to make the patient feel better

explanation.surface: Something one indulges in to lift the mood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'good feeling' suggests cheerfulness, but it is health: medicine taken to make you feel well.
explanation.definitionFit: A pill is a dose of medicine swallowed to improve how a patient feels.

clue.text: One seen in a palace tour going round with Eric

indicators.note: the letters of tour and Eric go round, changing order

explanation.surface: A sightseer in a palace tour, going round with a friend called Eric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going round' looks like part of the sightseeing picture but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An attendant at a royal court is a person found in a palace.

clue.text: Challenge of opponent on the railway

explanation.surface: An opponent issuing a challenge while on a train.
explanation.definitionFit: Competition between contenders is a contest or challenge, a loose synonym.

clue.text: Radio set designed for a space traveller

indicators.note: the letters of Radio set are designed anew in a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A radio set built for an astronaut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'space traveller' suggests an astronaut; it is a rocky body orbiting the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: A minor planet moves through space around the sun, so it is a traveller in space.

clue.text: Easter break for her

indicators.note: the word Easter is broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: An Easter holiday arranged for a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Easter break' reads as a holiday, but 'break' rearranges EASTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's given name, so it can stand for 'her'.

clue.text: Translated Belgian language

indicators.note: the letters of Belgian are translated into another arrangement

explanation.surface: Something Belgian rendered into another tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: The tongue of Bangladesh and West Bengal is a language.

clue.text: Recognise a refusal when you hear it

indicators.note: what is heard is a word sounding like the refusal

explanation.surface: Advice to spot a refusal when it comes.
explanation.definitionFit: To recognise someone or something is to be acquainted with it.

clue.text: Head for a beating but don't turn back

definitions.text: Head for a beating but don't turn back

parts.words: Head for a beating but don't turn back
parts.note: to look a coming loss in the eye, heading toward it instead of turning tail

explanation.surface: Someone marching on toward a thrashing without retreating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'don't turn back' points to the first word: you keep your front to something, not your back.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means to confront a likely loss head-on, keeping one's front toward it.

clue.text: English flier — a friend for ever

parts.note: a tern is a seabird, so a flier

explanation.surface: An English pilot who is a friend for life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flier' suggests a pilot; it is a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Lasting without end, which is what for ever means.

clue.text: Certain to be above zero

definitions.meaning: a number greater than nought has a plus sign

explanation.surface: Someone sure they will finish above nought.
explanation.definitionFit: Being sure is one sense; numbers greater than nought form the mathematical sense.

clue.text: Record our time and dampen spirits

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Documenting our era turns out to be depressing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Record' looks like a verb, but it is the noun: a disc.
explanation.definitionFit: To dishearten is to dampen someone's spirits.

clue.text: Failure of French umpire's tennis call

parts.note: fault is called when a serve misses the service box

explanation.surface: A French umpire's mistaken call at a tennis match.
explanation.definitionFit: A failure to pay or to act as required, as in a missed loan payment.

clue.text: He is brave, so was she

definitions.text: He is brave, so was she

parts.words: He is brave, so was she
parts.note: a brave man earns this title; so did the priestess loved by Leander in Greek legend

explanation.surface: A tribute to a brave couple.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'she' is Hero of Greek myth, whose lover Leander swam the Hellespont nightly to meet her.
explanation.definitionFit: A brave man is called this, and it was also the name of Leander's beloved priestess.

clue.text: Speed too much and exceed limit

definitions.meaning: to run past a mark by going too fast
to go beyond a set time or budget

explanation.surface: A driver going too fast and breaking the limit.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean going past an intended boundary, whether by racing past a mark or running over time or cost.

clue.text: Holy man to look for water

definitions.meaning: to dowse, searching for underground springs with a rod

explanation.surface: A priest goes searching for water.
explanation.definitionFit: A noun meaning a cleric, and a verb for discovering hidden water by dowsing.

clue.text: Building frame

definitions.meaning: the structure of a building, as in a church's upkeep fund
the basic framework or structure of something

explanation.definitionFit: The word means a building's physical structure and, more generally, any framework or makeup.

clue.text: The base of a cocktail might, to start with

definitions.text: The base of a cocktail might, to start with

parts.words: The base of a cocktail might, to start with
parts.note: the clue completes as a sentence: the spirit at the base of a cocktail might ..., and the run of letters means start

explanation.surface: A bartender musing on what goes into a cocktail first.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as 'be gin': the base of a cocktail might be gin. Read whole, it means to start.
explanation.definitionFit: To commence is a plain synonym of to start.

clue.text: Union gets a nice settlement after all

indicators.note: the rearranged letters come after the word all
the letters of a nice are settled into a new order

explanation.surface: A union reaches a pleasant deal after everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'settlement' reads as the union's deal, but it is the anagram signal; 'after' places the shuffled letters behind the first word.
explanation.definitionFit: A pact between partners or nations is a union.

clue.text: I leave Elsie instead

indicators.note: the letter I leaves the name Elsie

explanation.surface: Someone saying they'll go and leave Elsie in their place.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as in 'or else', meaning otherwise, alternatively or instead.

clue.text: Drunk in an ugly situation gets awkward

indicators.note: the letters of in an ugly stagger drunkenly into a new order

explanation.surface: A drunk in a nasty scene ends up clumsy.
explanation.definitionFit: Clumsy and lacking grace is a synonym of awkward.

clue.text: Farmer at the helm?

definitions.meaning: the bar used to steer a boat, found at the helm

explanation.surface: A farmer taking charge of a boat or company.
explanation.definitionFit: One who cultivates land, and the steering lever of a boat.

clue.text: Offered to alter the rent deed

indicators.note: the letters of rent deed are altered into a different order

explanation.surface: A tenant offering to change the lease.
explanation.definitionFit: To present a bid or resignation formally is to offer it.

clue.text: Know about any transported from East Africa

parts.note: ken is an old word meaning to know or have knowledge of

indicators.note: the letters of any are moved into a new order

explanation.surface: An expert on anything carried out of East Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transported' rearranges ANY to YAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen of the country on Africa's eastern coast, so someone from East Africa.
